clue.text: Relaxed after a couple of pages, satisfied

indicators.note: after places the word for relaxed behind the A and the two pages

parts.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for page, so two pages give PP
relaxed or loosened means eased

explanation.surface: Someone calms down and feels content after reading a couple of pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to pacify them, leaving them content.

clue.text: The sponsor's two little boys

definitions.note: read as 'the sponsor is', the 's being a link

parts.note: Pat is a short boy's name
Ron is another short boy's name

explanation.surface: A sponsor's family turns out to be just two small sons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little boys' means boys' names in short form: PAT (Patrick) and RON (Ronald). The 's after sponsor stands for 'is' and links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron backs an artist or cause financially, which is what a sponsor does.

clue.text: Quits when rugby game doesn't start

indicators.note: the word for the rugby game loses its opening letter

parts.note: sevens is the seven-a-side form of rugby

explanation.surface: A player calls it a day when the rugby match fails to kick off.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVENS is rugby played seven a side; 'doesn't start' removes its first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means neither side owes the other anything, so the score is level.

clue.text: What's the point of getting married in far-flung colonies?

indicators.note: in puts the married abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
far-flung suggests the letters of colonies scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A cynic asks why anyone would bother getting wed in remote overseas colonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's the point' reads as a shrug but is the definition: this mark is a point over a comma. 'far-flung' makes SEICOLON, and 'in' sets the M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark is a dot above a comma, so it is literally a point in writing.

clue.text: Everything from the kitchen sink up here

definitions.text: Everything from the kitchen sink up here

parts.words: Everything from the kitchen sink up here
parts.note: the washed crockery and pans taken out of the sink are stacked up on this rack to dry

explanation.definitionFit: A dish rack beside the sink holds washed items while the water runs off them.

clue.text: Overlook purchase, say, after exam success

indicators.note: after puts the sounded word behind the exam result

parts.note: to pass is to succeed in an exam

indicators.note: say signals a word that is spoken, giving the sound of buy

parts.note: a purchase is a buy

explanation.surface: A student treats themselves to a shopping trip once their exam is passed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something by is to ignore or neglect it, missing it out.

clue.text: The risk for every single pound

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A gambler weighs up what is at stake on each pound wagered.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is danger, the chance of harm.

clue.text: Discharge soldiers in division

indicators.note: in puts the soldiers inside the word for division

parts.note: a section is a division of something
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Troops are dismissed from service within an army division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a military verb; here it is a noun, something the body discharges.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretion is a substance released by a gland, such as sweat or saliva.

clue.text: Medical applications from groups admitting maturity

indicators.note: admitting means taking in, so the word for maturity goes inside the word for groups

parts.note: bands are groups, of musicians or people
age means maturity, as in coming of age

explanation.surface: Hospital forms are filed by age group when patients are admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandages are dressings wrapped onto wounds, applied by medics.

clue.text: The flow of runs in second eleven?

indicators.note: in puts the runs abbreviation inside the word for eleven

parts.note: a team of eleven, in cricket or football
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator wonders about the run rate of the reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' suggests a reserve cricket side; it splits into S (second) and TEAM (eleven).
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a current of water, a steady flow.

clue.text: Can Farsi be interpreted by these people?

indicators.note: interpreted suggests the letters of the two words are rendered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about whether a group can understand the Persian language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be interpreted' rearranges CAN FARSI; the definition is 'these people'.
explanation.definitionFit: Africans are people from the continent of Africa.

clue.text: Befuddled Costa rican at missing islander

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters are mixed up
missing tells us the letters of at are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A confused man from Costa Rica is lost and absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of COSTA RICAN, remove A and T ('missing'), and rearrange the rest ('Befuddled').
explanation.definitionFit: A Corsican lives on Corsica, a Mediterranean island.

clue.text: Freedom to move with little backing in place

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the word for place

parts.note: to lay is to place or put down

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for little is turned round

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Someone has a bit of room to manoeuvre if they reverse into a space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns WEE into EEW, which goes 'in' LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is latitude, the scope to act without restriction.

clue.text: Roger is given a warm welcome

explanation.surface: A man named Roger is greeted warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like a name but is radio talk for 'message understood'.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio jargon the reply means your message got through clearly; a guest greeted warmly has been met with approval.

clue.text: Reclusive, having been scratched

explanation.surface: Someone shy of company after getting clawed by a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratched' here means removed from a race or contest, as a horse is.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy person keeps to themselves; a horse pulled out of a race before the start is scratched.

clue.text: One tried here to give space to romance

parts.note: to court is to woo or romance someone
room means space

explanation.surface: A couple tries making room in their lives for love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One tried' means a defendant on trial, not someone making an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Defendants are put on trial in a hall of the law courts.

clue.text: Not worried — there's no charge for nursing!

parts.note: nursing is care of the sick
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is relieved that nursing treatment costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to free medical care in the UK's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without anxieties is untroubled and relaxed.

clue.text: Run into waste disposal queue

indicators.note: disposal suggests arranging, as in at your disposal, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone lines up to use the rubbish chute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposal' rearranges RUN INTO WASTE; 'queue' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To queue is to stand in line until it is your go.

clue.text: Skinhead wearing a toupée drank heavily

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of skin is S
someone in a toupee is wigged, wearing a hairpiece

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed man in a hairpiece knocked back his drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' is read as the head of 'skin', its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To swig is to gulp a drink in large mouthfuls.

clue.text: A time trial might provide evidence

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A timed cycling race could yield proof of someone's form.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness, declaring something true.

clue.text: Paid attention to a couple of journalists chasing ambassador

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the journalists come after the ambassador

parts.note: HE is His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: a couple of means two, so the journalist abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Reporters pursuing a diplomat took careful note of what was said.
explanation.walkthrough: HE (His Excellency) is a crossword convention for ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to take notice of it.

clue.text: Push for access to the house

explanation.surface: Someone presses for a way into the home.
explanation.definitionFit: To push hard is to propel or urge; a private road leading up to a home is its driveway.

clue.text: Suggest that prisoner takes it back

indicators.note: takes means the prisoner holds the turned word inside

parts.note: an inmate is a prisoner

indicators.note: back means the word it is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner is told to withdraw a remark he made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives TI, which the prisoner 'takes' inside; 'Suggest' is a verb here, to hint at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to hint or imply something indirectly.

clue.text: Theologian dismissed from midland's city

indicators.note: dismissed from means the theologian's letters are removed from the word midland

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A churchman is removed from his post in an English Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Ds are taken out separately, one from the middle and one from the end of MIDLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Not looking forward to lecture on Germany

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the lecture word after the Germany abbreviation

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a reading can be a lecture, as a university reader gives

explanation.surface: A student is apprehensive about a lecture on German history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like 'about'; it is a placing word, putting READING after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreading means fearing something that is coming.

clue.text: Well informed workers?

parts.note: workers who know all about wells, the drilled kind that produce crude

explanation.definitionFit: These workers drill and operate petroleum wells.

clue.text: Intend to ignore heartless miserly person

parts.note: to mean is to intend

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters of ignore are removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A stingy person plans to coldly disregard someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a stingy, ungenerous person.

clue.text: Admit one might perhaps hold sway

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A ruler concedes that someone else may be in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ADMIT ONE; 'might' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to rule or have control over others.
